title: Pricing a Resort Lodging Stay That Straddles Two Published Rate Windows
content:
Where a Resort Lodging stay straddles two published rate windows, the mix of its nights decides how it is priced.

Where more than half of the nights of the stay fall inside the higher priced of the two windows it straddles, every night of the stay is priced at that window's nightly rate and those nightly amounts are added together.

Where half or fewer of the nights of the stay fall inside the higher priced of the two windows it straddles, every night of the stay is priced at the lower window's nightly rate and those nightly amounts are added together.

Where every night of the stay falls inside one published rate window, each night is priced on the published rate window it falls in and those nightly amounts are added together.

## The published windows the nights are read against

The holiday window runs from the 19th of December 2026 to the 2nd of January 2027 inclusive. The peak window runs from the 3rd of January 2027 to the 14th of March 2027 inclusive. A night falling in neither lies outside both published windows. The two windows a stay straddles are therefore the two its nights actually fall in, and of those two the higher priced is the one carrying the higher nightly rate for the unit type.

| Mix of the nights of the stay | How the nights are priced |
| --- | --- |
| More than half inside the higher priced window it straddles | every night at the higher window's nightly rate |
| Half or fewer inside the higher priced window it straddles | every night at the lower window's nightly rate |
| Every night inside one published window | each night on the window it falls in |

### Both sides of the halfway mark (hypothetical stays)

A stay of 6 nights of which 4 fall inside the holiday window and 2 fall outside both windows straddles the holiday window and the window of the nights outside it. More than half of the 6 nights fall inside the higher priced of the two, so all 6 nights are priced at the holiday nightly rate.

A stay of 6 nights of which 3 fall inside the holiday window and 3 fall outside both windows has half, not more than half, of its nights inside the higher priced window, so all 6 nights are priced at the lower window's nightly rate.

A stay of 6 nights every one of which falls inside the peak window straddles nothing, so each of the 6 nights is priced on the peak window it falls in.
